messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — nightly hetero-gpu CI failing on beam-search jobs across 3 shards. Repro shows CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS from kernel call during kv-cache expand. Full log:
```
E 2025-11-20 03:12:11 beam_search.cpp:412 cudaMemcpyAsync -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
stack: ...
NVRM: Xid 13
```
ci-bot: job: https://ci.redwood/invocations/54321 nightly/gpu/het/54321 failed on node gpunode-17 — artifacts: /artifacts/54321/logs.tar.gz
ton y: Can you paste nvidia-smi from the node and container info? suspect driver/lib mismatch after a host update.
lee: Also check dmesg for NVRM messages and `modinfo nvidia`.
maria: running quick checks: on host `nvidia-smi` shows Driver Version: 535.86.05; in container `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so` points to CUDA 12.1 libs. minimal repro command I tried:
```
docker run --gpus all -it --rm --entrypoint /bin/bash redwood/llm-infer:canary -c "./repro.sh --seq 2048"
```
Output crashed with same illegal address.
sasha: That combo would explain it — kernel module 535.* vs container runtime expecting 540.*? Also curious if host kernel was upgraded on gpunode-17 last night.
maria: `modinfo nvidia | grep version` -> `version: 535.86.05`
tony: infra, were there driver/kernel module updates rolled last night on that pool?
infra-bot: Rolling updates ran 2025-11-20 02:50 UTC on pool-gpu-us-west-2; driver package v535.86 installed to hosts. No container images were rebuilt.
lee: If the module got upgraded, containers expecting older PTX can crash. Try running the container with `--gpus all --env NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all --rm` and mount host libcuda: `-v /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1:ro` to force consistent libcuda.
maria: did that — still reproduce. dmesg shows:
```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID 10234: GPU access fault, reason unknown.
```
sasha: let's cordon the node and schedule a targeted canary with pinned driver image. Also grab `journalctl -k` and `dmesg -T` outputs for the node.
tony: I'll open a quick infra ticket and pin the nightly to a node running previous driver 535.54 for one run. If that passes, we'll know it's module-related.
infra-bot: Ticket INFRA-1372 created. Node gpunode-17 cordoned. Canaries scheduled: nightly/het/54321-retry pinned -> running.
maria: repro run in pinned node passed 3/3 shards. Looks good. I'll collect core dumps and upload logs to /artifacts/54321/driver-investigation/.
lee: Suggest we add an early CI check to mismatch-detect: compare host `nvidia-smi` driver vs container cuda runtime major/minor and fail fast with clear message.
sasha: agree. If infra can avoid rolling drivers without rebuilds, that helps too. I'll draft a short postmortem blurb.
maria: thanks all. :thumbsup: I'll follow up with artifacts link and mark ticket INFRA-1372 resolved after verification.
